extracted.intended_audience: Investigators preparing an NIH R15 (AREA) grant application / PDs-PIs and grant reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and responding to reviewer critiques for an NIH R15 (PA-16-200) research grant application, including Research Plan (Specific Aims, Research Strategy), budget and compliance attachments. Focus is on justifying significance, innovation, approach, budgets, and required compliance sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance (NIH review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assesses whether the project addresses an important problem and the broader implications/impact. Reviewer raised concerns that a small number of annual cases reduces enthusiasm; PI must explain why the problem is important (e.g., underreporting, epidemic potential, chronic Q fever morbidity, limited current therapies) and the broader implications and institutional impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain epidemiological relevance and public health importance; tie the study to broader fields (e.g., comparative studies with Francisella/Rickettsia), and explicitly describe impact on the institution, including student-training benefits (addressed in Facilities & Resources and student-training plan).

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation (NIH review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluates novelty of concepts, approaches and whether the project challenges current paradigms. Reviewer noted that examining horizontal gene transfer (HGT) in Coxiella is new to the system but that HGT is a well-understood phenomenon and some methods may be standard practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize the novel aspects (e.g., central hypothesis that C. burnetii evolved via massive HGT, novel tRNA-based virulence mechanism, and overcoming technical barriers to genome-scale functional studies). Provide explicit statements (and Table 1) that clarify how the project departs from standard practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach (NIH review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assesses the rigor, feasibility, and appropriateness of methods. Reviewers questioned reliance on KEGG/other databases for function assignment and potential confounds (e.g., presence of tRNAGlu1 affecting interpretation of heme-biosynthesis essentiality).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide methodological details and contingency plans (e.g., not relying on databases for single-gene function calls but for pathway-level inference; experimental validation such as complementation tests for deletion strains; using transposon-mutant libraries, RNA-seq comparisons, and intracellular vs ACCM-2 growth assays to validate findings). Address potential confounds explicitly and show how planned experiments resolve them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan for prioritizing candidate genes/pathways
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers requested a clear plan for prioritizing genes/pathways identified in Aims 1 and 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PI's stated prioritization: (1) pathways for synthesis of critical metabolites not obtainable from the host (e.g., heme, biotin), (2) pathways for metabolizing critical nutrients (e.g., glutamate), (3) proteins required for homeostasis (e.g., Na+/H+ antiporters). Include a prioritization table (Table 1) and justify choices based on expected impact and feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linking Aim 1 discoveries to Aim 2 characterization
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer asked whether genes identified in comparative genomics (Aim 1) will be characterized in functional studies (Aim 2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define explicit criteria for selecting targets from Aim 1 for Aim 2 (e.g., pathogen-specific pathways that contain HGT-derived genes). Use phylogenetic methods to identify HGT-derived candidates and employ RNA-seq and transposon-insertion libraries to validate importance to intracellular growth. State prioritization strategy (pathway overlap between Aims 1 & 2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiating metabolic genes from genes required for entry/replication/general survival
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer asked how the proposal will distinguish genes required for metabolism from those required for other aspects of infection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare gene expression and mutant phenotypes between intracellular growth and growth in ACCM-2 medium; test transposon mutants in both conditions to identify genes specifically critical for intracellular growth versus general viability or entry/replication functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan for hypothetical (unannotated) genes
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer asked what will be done with hypothetical genes identified in genomic analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State prioritization policy: treat hypothetical genes as lower priority initially and focus resources on high-confidence, annotated metabolic targets; note that hypothetical genes may be revisited if they show strong differential expression or transposon phenotypes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims structure and expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: The application must clearly state long-term goals, a central hypothesis, specific aims, and expected outcomes. The example lists three aims: (1) identify metabolic pathways distinguishing C. burnetii from tick-associated Coxiella, (2) define pathways critical to intracellular growth using phylogenetics/RNA-seq/transposon libraries, (3) experimentally validate heme biosynthesis importance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make aims concise, hypothesis-driven, and feasible within the budget/period. Describe expected outcomes and how they enable future translational applications (e.g., drug targets such as HemA/HemL).

rubrics_metrics.name: PHS 398 Research Plan required components
rubrics_metrics.description: The Research Plan submission must include specific labeled sections/attachments: Introduction (for resubmissions), Specific Aims, Research Strategy, Progress Report Publication List, Protection of Human Subjects, Data Safety Monitoring Plan, Inclusion of Women and Minorities, Inclusion of Children, Vertebrate Animals, Select Agent Research, Multiple PD/PI Leadership Plan, Consortium/Contractual Arrangements, Letters of Support, Resource Sharing Plan(s), Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources, and Appendix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide each required document as a separate attachment (filenames shown) and ensure all compliance and reporting sections are completed per PHS 398 instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget form structure and line-item requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Budget must be entered in RESEARCH & RELATED Budget sections A-K: Senior/Key Person (A), Other Personnel (B), Equipment (C; list items exceeding $5,000), Travel (D), Participant/Trainee Support (E), Other Direct Costs (F), Direct Costs total (G), Indirect Costs (H; specify type, rate, base), Total Direct and Indirect (I), Fee (J) and Budget Justification (K).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide organization DUNS, budget type (Project/Subaward), project dates, personnel months, requested salaries, fringe, funds requested per line, list equipment > $5,000, and upload one Budget Justification file. Ensure totals reconcile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget Justification content expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Budget justification must explain personnel roles and effort, supplies, sequencing and RNA-seq costs, travel, publication costs, and indirect cost calculations. Example details: PI commits 3 summer months/year; Research Associate 4.80 calendar months (0.40 FTE); GRAs and undergraduates summer months and hourly wage ($12/hr, ~69.5 hrs/mo); specific fringe benefit rates (PI/postdoc 30%, GRAs/undergrads 9%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide monthly effort (calendar months/FTE) for each person, link student projects to thesis aims, justify sequencing and other consumable costs, include travel support for student meeting attendance, estimate publication page charges, and apply institutional negotiated F&A rate with calculation method (MTDC exclusions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect costs / F&A rate disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Indirect costs must be calculated per the institution's federally negotiated rate agreement (example: MTDC base at 48.5%). Provide cognizant federal agency contact (name, phone).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the indirect cost rate, the base used (MTDC), and include the cognizant agency contact. Apply MTDC exclusions correctly (e.g., tuition, equipment over threshold).

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Subjects protections and clinical trial reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Application must state whether the project involves human subjects and whether it is a clinical trial (Agency-defined Phase III?). Include Protection of Human Subjects section and Data Safety Monitoring Plan if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate Yes/No on clinical trial, complete Protection of Human Subjects, and include a DSM plan when human subjects are involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate animal use reporting and euthanasia method compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Vertebrate Animals section must indicate whether vertebrate animals are used and whether they are euthanized. If euthanasia is used, indicate consistency with AVMA guidelines or provide justification for deviation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer the vertebrate animal questions, and if euthanasia is used, affirm AVMA-consistent methods or supply scientific justification and details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human embryonic stem cell (hESC) compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: If the project involves hESCs, list registration number(s) from the NIH registry or indicate a plan to use a registry-listed line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include registry numbers (e.g., '0004') or check the box committing to use a registry-listed line when specific line cannot be referenced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventions and patents disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Declare whether the project has inventions or patents and whether previously reported on prior progress reports (renewal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer Yes/No and provide details if Yes, following renewal reporting instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change of Investigator / Change of Institution reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is a change of PD/PI or grantee institution, provide former PD/PI name or former institution name and required fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete the Change of Investigator/Institution section with former PD/PI or institution details as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission introduction and point-by-point responses
rubrics_metrics.description: For resubmissions, include an Introduction that responds to reviewer critiques and states how the revised proposal addresses concerns; mark changes clearly (e.g., in blue).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide point-by-point replies to each reviewer comment, indicate where revisions have been made in the application (e.g., Facilities & Resources, Table 1), and include supporting modifications in the Research Strategy and other sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select Agent Research disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: If the proposed work involves select agents, include a Select Agent Research section/attachment (example file: select_agents-R15-2016-resub.pdf).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose select agent use and include required documentation and biosafety approvals per FOA instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: AREA (R15) student-training and institutional impact
rubrics_metrics.description: For AREA/R15 proposals, reviewers consider the impact of the award on student research and institutional research capacity; reviewer questioned clarity of impact on the institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly describe how the award will enhance student training (student training plans at end of each Aim), detail expected student involvement/presentations at meetings, and show how funding will build institutional research capacity (e.g., startup, collaborations).
